scope: Iroh ALPN routing, Raft auth negotiation, proxy/federation handshakes, blob/DAG/docs/snapshot-style streaming assumptions, rate limits, and metrics drift

finding.summary: The production aspen-node router did not register RAFT_AUTH_ALPN when config.iroh.enable_raft_auth was set, while the Raft network factory selects authenticated outbound ALPN under the same config.
remediation: Register RAFT_AUTH_ALPN for NodeMode::Single when config.iroh.enable_raft_auth is true.
Register RAFT_AUTH_ALPN for primary-shard NodeMode::Sharded when config.iroh.enable_raft_auth is true.
Seed TrustedPeersRegistry with local Iroh public key and start spawn_membership_watcher for membership-derived peer keys.

audited_assumptions.evidence: connection_pool/pool_management.rs selects RAFT_AUTH_ALPN when use_auth_alpn is true and warns for legacy RAFT_ALPN fallback.
setup_router now gates RAFT_AUTH_ALPN registration on config.iroh.enable_raft_auth in both single and primary-shard modes.
proxy.rs is reached through client RPC handler context and uses verified-token handoff rather than a standalone unauthenticated ALPN.
registration remains feature/config gated with explicit cluster identity and TrustManager setup before accept.
registration is feature/resource gated; deeper bulk-stream rate-limit and authorization semantics remain follow-up scope.

known_unrelated_failures: cargo check --bin aspen-node --features full currently fails in aspen-wasm-plugin due to missing aspen_core::app_registry and aspen_core::ServiceExecutor API paths.
residual_risk: Legacy RAFT_ALPN remains registered for backward compatibility even when auth is enabled.
Bulk transfer rate limiting for snapshot/blob/DAG streams needs a deeper follow-up slice.
